column69: It’s weird for us Spanish speakers to use “;” to connect two different phrases in one. Either you use a concrete preposition or you use verbs, which adds to the fluidity of the phrase. In this case, only some of the examples had that and that’s what got most of them lesser grades in fluidity than significance. On top of that, there are certain syntax differences in how we build our adjectives into a phrase. Eg. in English “clean white table” could refer to the characteristics of the colour, but also just to the appearance of the table. In Spanish, since it added a “y” (“and”), it got directly translated into what would be “a white and clean table”. If we’re talking about colour, an appropriate way would be “una mesa de color blanco limpio”. Basically it depends on what you’re actually trying to convey.
